summary: No (a) or (d) flags. All seven request items are answered, not merely gestured at. I recomputed every stated figure independently and all match: radian ratios 0.9983342 / 0.9999833 / 0.9999998 → 1; degree ratios 0.01745241 / 0.01745328 / 0.01745329 → π/180 ≈ 0.0174533, with the conversion-factor identity sin(h°)/h = [sin(πh/180)/(πh/180)]·(π/180) given as the reason; (b) sin(π/3+0.01) = 0.8709820, forward difference 0.49566 vs cos(π/3) = 0.5, gap −0.00434 with the correct sign, explained as chord-vs-tangent truncation ≈ −(h/2)sin(π/3) = −0.00433, reduced by smaller h (0.499567 at h = 0.001) or the central difference 0.4999917 (gap −0.0000083, about 520× smaller); (c) the squeeze argument is reproduced with the three areas ½sinθ ≤ ½θ ≤ ½tanθ, the sector line explicitly identified as the only place radian measure enters (degree version πθ/360 → limit π/180), evenness covers negative h, and L'Hôpital and the Maclaurin series are both flagged as circular without claiming L'Hôpital is forbidden at HL; (d) d/dx sin(x°) = (π/180)cos(x°) via the chain rule, linked to the horizontal stretch, with a worked value at x = 60; the Cotes (1714) and Thomson (Belfast, 1873) attributions are hedged as 'usually credited', tagged 'recalled, not consulted', name a real reference (Cajori vol. 2, 1929; MacTutor) without inventing journal issues or page numbers, and the IB rationale is given with a check-your-booklet hedge. The underlying question (unit changes the function's horizontal scale, every gradient scaled by π/180) is answered directly in the opening paragraph. No marks were awarded, so no provisional label was required; the Sources line is present and tagged. One non-flag cosmetic note: in (b) the intermediate '−0.0000499996/0.01 = −0.0049999583' displays a 10 d.p.-rounded numerator while the quotient uses the unrounded value; the result is correct.
